fields.features_heading: What the Registrar Needs Before Opening Day
fields.features_subheading: A spring sign-up decides who plays, in which division, and who works the concession stand. Parents answer all of it on one form.
fields.feature_1:
League age worked out from one birth date

Parents enter a birth date and choose a program. The form counts the age on August 31 of the current year for baseball and on December 31 of the previous year for softball.
fields.feature_2:
A division set by your own age bands

Tell the form which league ages play in which division, such as 9 and 10 in Minors. The confirmation names the division, and the board sees a count for every division.
fields.feature_3:
Residency proof read on upload

Parents upload one or more documents from each of the three groups Little League lists. The app reads the address on every file, and a scan it cannot read goes to the registrar.
fields.feature_4:
Brothers and sisters on one registration

A parent types the address and phone number once, then adds each child with a birth date and a program. A brother in baseball and a sister in softball share one confirmation.
fields.feature_5:
Volunteer shifts claimed during sign-up

Set how many concession stand shifts the season needs and how many each family takes. The volunteer coordinator gets an email when a family claims the last open shift.
fields.feature_6:
Player records in a database you own

Every registration saves as a row in a database you own, with no response caps. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep building on it.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Jobs the Form Does at Juniper Flats
fields.tab_content_1:
A July 19 birthday puts Lachlan in Minors

Juniper Flats Little League puts league ages 9 and 10 in Minors for the 2027 season. Lachlan Ruvalcaba was born on July 19, 2017, which makes him 10 on August 31. His mother, Marisol, enters that birth date, and the form places him in Minors. Her confirmation email names the division.
fields.tab_content_2:
Softball counts Ingrid's age from last December

Ingrid Deverell was born on April 22, 2016. Under the baseball date she would play the 2027 season at 11. Softball counts her age on December 31, 2026, when she was still 10, so the form places her in Softball Minors with the other players of league age 9 and 10.
fields.tab_content_3:
One blurry scan goes to the registrar

Della Brightmore uploads one document from each of the three residency groups. The app reads 418 Quarry Bend Road from two of them, the same address she typed on the form. Her Group 2 scan is too blurry to read. It goes to registrar Anselm Nadeau, who checks it by hand before he confirms her son's spot.
fields.tab_content_4:
Pilar hears that all 120 shifts are covered

Juniper Flats needs 120 concession stand shifts this season, 2 from each of its 60 families. Parents pick their shifts on the last page of the form. When the Ostergaard family takes the final pair, volunteer coordinator Pilar Kitteridge gets an email that all 120 are covered, and the schedule closes.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Little League Registration Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build a Little League registration form that sets each player's league age and checks residency before the season.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the divisions your board runs
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for the birth date, not the age
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every division for the season with the league ages it takes, such as 11 and 12 in Majors. Keep baseball and softball on separate lists, because the two programs count league age from different dates.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask parents for each player's birth date and program, and let the form work out league age from it. The confirmation screen then names the division before the parent leaves the page.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for documents from all three groups on the residency list, each dated or in force inside the window it sets. Decide who reviews a scan the app cannot read, such as the league registrar.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put the parent's address and phone number at the top of the form, then let the parent add each child below. Every child gets a birth date, a program, and a division under one family record.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the divisions, the age dates, the residency step, and the volunteer shifts into one prompt. Emergent builds the form, the database behind it and a dashboard for the board, and you change any part later by prompting.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Register one player with a July birthday, a softball player born in the spring, and a family with a blurry upload. Check every division against your age chart, and confirm the blurry scan reaches the registrar.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Post the link where families look
fields.howto_step_7_des: Share the link on the league website and in the email to last season's families. Close registration on the date your board sets. Every division is then final before teams are formed.

faq_plan.q: What is a Little League registration form?
faq_plan.a: A Little League registration form is how a local league signs players up for a season. Parents give the player's name and birth date, plus their own contact details and proof of residency. The league uses the birth date to set each player's league age, and the league age decides the division.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a Little League registration form?
faq_plan.a: List your divisions with their league ages, decide which residency documents to collect, and set the volunteer shifts each family takes. Describe all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. It builds the form and the database behind it, and the free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: Which fields belong on a Little League registration form?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the player's full name, birth date, and program. Then collect the parent's contact details and home address before the residency uploads. Leave age off the form. The birth date gives the league age, and the form names the division from it.

faq_plan.q: Can one Little League registration form cover siblings?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Put the parent's details at the top, then a repeating block that holds each child's birth date and program. Build it that way instead of as a one-player registration form, and a family of three types its address once. With Emergent, every child saves as a row under one family in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How does a Little League registration form work out league age?
faq_plan.a: It takes the birth date and applies the date for the program the parent picks. Little League sets a baseball player's league age by how old the child is on August 31 of the season year. Softball looks back to December 31 of the year before, which makes a player born between January and August a year younger in softball than in baseball. Parents never do that math themselves.

faq_plan.q: Which residency documents should a Little League registration form collect?
faq_plan.a: At least one document from every group on Little League's three-group residency list. Every document shows the parent or guardian's name and full address, dated or in force between February 1 of the previous year and February 1 of the current year. Link your league's current checklist beside the upload step, and give parents one upload box per group.

faq_plan.q: Can a winter hitting class use the Little League registration form?
faq_plan.a: It works better as its own form in the same app. A weekly hitting class needs session dates and a roster for each class instead of divisions, which is the job of a class registration form. Emergent builds it from a prompt, and you change either form later by prompting.

faq_plan.q: Can a Little League registration form include volunteer shifts?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add a shift picker after the player details. Give it the total the season needs and the number per family, and hide a shift once a family claims it. When the last one goes, the app emails your volunteer coordinator that the schedule is full.

faq_plan.q: Can parents fill out a Little League registration form on a phone?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A parent can complete it on a phone and photograph residency documents straight into the upload step. If your league still posts a Little League registration form PDF, keep it for families who ask for paper, and type those entries into the same table by hand.

faq_plan.q: Should a parents' meeting held online go on the Little League registration form?
faq_plan.a: No, give it its own form. A preseason parents' meeting held online needs a time, a join link, and a reminder, with no birth dates or divisions to work out. A webinar registration form handles that, and the player form stays short.
